newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian woman burned, estranged husband sought.
newsitem.headline: Canadian woman burned, estranged husband sought.

text.p: A Canadian woman suffered severe burns to most of her body after being doused with flammable liquid and set afire early on Monday by a man police believe was her estranged husband.

The 23-year-old woman was in a hospital in critical and unstable condition, police said. Her children, aged two, three and four, were sent to the hospital for smoke inhalation after the fire engulfed a bedroom at the family's townhouse in north Edmonton.
Police said the woman and a male friend were in the living room of the home at 4 a.m. when an intruder crept in and poured a substance smelling like gasoline over both of them.
The male friend then ran to a neighbor's house where police were called. He ran away without his shirt and shoes but was later picked up by police.
Moments later, the woman and the home's master bedroom caught fire, police said. The intruder, believed to be the woman's ex-husband, fled and had not been found by police.
"There had been in the past a history of spousal violence," Edmonton Police spokeswoman Annette Bidniak said. "It's bizarre to say the least. We just hope we're able to get to the bottom of it."
